newsitem.title: SPAIN: FCC, Dragados shares rise, FCC denies merger.
newsitem.headline: FCC, Dragados shares rise, FCC denies merger.

text.p: Spain's Fomento de Construcciones denied on Friday that it plans to merge with Dragados, while shares in both contractors were near all time highs and the rumour continued to circulate, dealers said.
"We deny that we are studing any possible merger. There are absolutely no plans in this sense," the FCC spokesman said.

A dealer at a foreign brokerage who requested anonymity said: "People have been talking about a merger or FCC taking a majority stake in Dragados, and they've also been talking about (19 percent stakeholder) BCH trying to stoke up the price (of Dragados)."
At 1135 GMT, Dragados was up 10 pesetas to 3,460 pesetas, having risen around eight percent on Thursday. FCC was up 210 pesetas, 1.11 percent, to 19,050, off an early high of 19,900.
The Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 0.31 percent to 6,694.28.
An analyst at a Spanish bank said it was possible, and had been for some time, that either construction firm bought a bigger stake in the other, but not at the moment.
"Independently of who takes who I would value it positively in terms of everything beyond Spanish construction," the analyst said.
"But a merger which affected business in Spain, to me, wouldn't make much sense. They'd lose market share because they'd lose their independent names, and both are big enough to stand alone here."
However, he saw any moves as unlikely at the moment.
"Dragados is still restructuring until the start of next year. It's cleaning up substantially and will make large savings...but further ties at this point could be chaotic," he added.
Both firms already have an agreement to develop business overseas, and last year FCC took a six percent stake of Dragados, while the latter took three percent of FCC.
Another factor thought to be affecting FCC was its planned four-for-one share split, for which no date has been announced, and which is due to be approved at the June 25 shareholders' meeting.
Construction stocks have rallied sharply this year amid a series of moves making the sector more concentrated, and a return of interest in cyclical firms.
